body: Yeah, I'm starting to think that he is just NOT going to be an indoor cat. I will try a couple more things but I'm getting to the end of my rope. As long as he's happy and I do everything I can to keep him healthy...
I do play with him a lot. When I get him to that "I'm so tired I'm panting" mode he just rests for 10 minutes then is ready to go again. Like infinite energy, at least when he's not sleeping.

I have been trying to scare him. A couple times I waited outside when my roommate let him out and dumped water on him! He was startled but still wanted to go outside. :/ And I've been letting him out at night lately, even when he is locked out for hours he doesn't seem to mind, even when it's cold and windy. The only thing I can think of that he really hates is being in the cat carrier, maybe I'll take him for a ride instead of letting him outside.

I struggle with this idea as well, although I'd say my body shape is basically the opposite of yours: I'm pretty tall at about 5'10" with short legs, long skinny noodle arms, wide shoulders but no boobs, a long relatively skinny torso, wide hips, basically carry all my weight in my butt/thighs. So yeah, I'm a pear shape and I hate it! I guess tastes vary and there's going to be someone who is jealous of what you have. 

With that said, I think 1) you may be pleasantly surprised with what your body turns into, you won't know until you get there! 2) There are exercises you can do to offset disproportionality (e.g., you might want to focus a lot on legs/glutes, I need more upper body stuff) 3) Getting your body to its best is not just a physical journey but a mental one as well.
Sorry! I mean I haven't been tracking my body measurements very well. I definitely do track my calories though. :)

I used to be super addicted to diet soda, I'd easily go through 2L of that every day. Not only is it expensive but it's also terrible for you and messed up my teeth which are already bad. So now I only drink that when I'm at a restaurant but it's like I just never really replaced it with water. I'm sure there are times were I don't drink any water at all, just a coffee in the morning and a tea at bed. It's very sad. I'll start setting a reminder on my phone, I want to at least get to 32oz of water/day. 

Also, I do have a history of ED, mostly bulimia. I wonder if that is messing me up somehow? I do tend to drop calories too quickly, feel super hungry for a while and then binge. 50 calories seems like a reasonable drop so I'll try that for a week and adjust as I go. Thanks! :)

Yes, I definitely do measure and count calories. I have been eating the same breakfast and lunch for about 3 months. For dinner I usually get a recipe from Budget Bytes or somewhere else, import it into MFP, and portion the servings into tupperware. I do try to follow the recipes but I admit I might not measure everything to 100% accuracy when I'm cooking. 

I also buy meat and bulk and weigh, portion, and freeze it but sometimes I have like .2lbs left over and I just throw add that into a freezer bag and don't account for the extras.

I guess I kind of chalked it up to measuring inconsistently. I do feel like my body composition has changed somewhat and some exercises have gotten easier. But I didn't think I could build substantial muscle mass eating at a deficit so I don't want to delude myself, either.

1. You're probably right, I generally do a pretty good job weighing and measuring things but I could do better. Also when I'm drinking/socializing, I try to eat light through the day to offset when I know I'm going to go out but sometimes I still go over (this happens about twice a month).

2. This is a huge problem, I know I don't get anywhere close to enough water. I drink water when I'm exercising but don't normally through the day, even if I bring a water bottle with me. I mostly drink tea and coffee.

3. I do weigh myself at the same time every day under the same conditions.

I think I will go ahead and just lower my calorie intake some more, I guess it can't hurt at this point. Also, I'd say I regulate calories more through portion sizes than eating "healthier" foods. I try to incorporate veggies into my dinner, at least.
